data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) to justify preferring corroborated theories without induction, but this concept was formally shown by David Miller and Tichý in 1974 to be undefined within Popper's own deductive framework unless one assumes a probabilistic distribution of truth over logical content. Since the target asserts the preference is defensible 'on Popper's own terms' while ignoring that Popper's specific definition of verisimilitude collapsed mathematically without smuggling in inductive assumptions, the claim that the preference avoids induction is false.
